claims.text: Phase field modeling can effectively predict high-temperature oxidation behavior and phase stability in materials exposed to oxidative environments.
Phase field modeling can be applied to alloys or ceramics in high-temperature oxidative environments.
Phase field modeling can simulate oxidation processes.
The modeled conditions can include high temperatures and varying oxygen partial pressures.
Oxidation involves microstructural evolution, including phase transformations and grain growth.
Phase field modeling captures the thermodynamics and kinetics of oxidation reactions.
Capturing oxidation thermodynamics and kinetics permits simulation of phase stability and oxidation behavior over time.
The model will predict changes in oxidation rates and phase stability.
Temperature, oxidation behavior, and material composition are correlated.
The proposed applicability is limited to high-temperature oxidative conditions and may not extend to lower temperatures or non-oxidative conditions.
The predictive accuracy of phase field modeling for oxidation behavior and phase stability is uncertain without empirical validation.
